headline: Disney+ and Hulu raise prices again as streaming inflation continues
summary: The ad-supported Disney+ tier now costs $12.49/month, with the ad-free Premium plan hitting $21.49/month. Hulu and bundle prices also increased.
details: Disney+ and Hulu have implemented another price increase, impacting subscribers for the second time in a year. The Basic plan with ads for Disney+ is now $12.49 per month, while the Premium ad-free tier has risen to $21.49 per month, marking a $2.50 increase.

This surge in subscription costs reflects the rising expenses associated with producing exclusive content and securing licensing rights. New subscribers will immediately face these higher prices, while existing subscribers will see the changes reflected on or after October 21, 2026.

When Disney+ first launched in 2019, its monthly price was a mere $6.99. Over the years, prices have steadily climbed, with an increase of $1 occurring a couple of years later. Even the ad-supported tier, introduced to offer a more affordable option, has seen its price raised.

This trend of price hikes is not unique to Disney+ or Hulu; many popular streaming services are following a similar pattern. As costs continue to escalate, consumers are increasingly evaluating the value proposition of each service, leading to subscription fatigue.

headline_marked: [[Claude.ai]] made 3x faster in two-week sprint using AI
headline: Claude.ai made 3x faster in two-week sprint using AI
summary: Anthropic used its own AI model to identify bottlenecks, build benchmarks, and ship over 3,000 changes to improve claude.ai performance.
details: Anthropic has significantly boosted the performance of its AI chatbot, Claude.ai, achieving a 3x speed improvement in just two weeks. The company utilized its own AI model, Claude, to identify performance bottlenecks, create benchmarks, and implement necessary changes.

The focus was on four key user journeys that constitute 95% of user activity. For instance, the time to load a typeable page on claude.ai dropped from 3.1 seconds to 0.55 seconds. Starting a new Claude Code session now takes 0.3 seconds, down from 0.8 seconds, and loading a Claude Cowork session improved from 2.6 seconds to 0.73 seconds.

To facilitate this rapid improvement, Anthropic created a dedicated Slack channel where Claude was tasked with monitoring deploys, assessing telemetry, maintaining dashboards, and proposing solutions. The AI was given the goal of becoming as autonomous as possible in managing performance.

Claude analyzed usage data to pinpoint the most impactful user journeys. The team then added instrumentation to establish comparable baselines for each journey, measuring from user interaction to result rendering and differentiating client-side from server-side work.

The sprint began with a list of hand-picked projects, each targeting a specific journey. Claude estimated the impact of these projects in milliseconds, helping the team set sprint targets. Many of these planned projects were completed ahead of schedule.

To accelerate launches, a static composer was integrated into the HTML, allowing users to type during React initialization. For the desktop app, a precompiled V8 code cache was implemented to prevent recompilation from scratch. Navigation was also improved by keeping the composer mounted between conversations and prefetching sessions.

The team also left room for Claude to identify new opportunities and propose additional workstreams. These emergent projects exceeded initial targets, leading to the implementation of new goals and further optimization efforts.

To iterate faster than their deploy cadence, Anthropic sought ways to measure performance in the lab. For JavaScript-heavy tasks, they measured literal instruction counts using Valgrind. For browser-based paths, they utilized deterministic counts like React commits per interaction and function call counts.
